items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was part of the guitar trio – Barney Kessel, Jim Hall, and myself – and I got beat up every night.

ctx.x: Because you were both on Columbia at this time. No, maybe – yeah, yeah.

That’s possible. We went on tour in 1967. He was voted the number one pianist in the jazz world. The tour was Thelonious and Sarah Vaughan, Barney Kessel, Jim Hall. I was part of the guitar trio – Barney Kessel, Jim Hall, and myself – and I got beat up every night. Those guys turned me every way but loose, and Barney Kessel just took it to the moon. He was so slick with his stuff. I admire him a lot. I always did. But being on tour with him was an awesome thing.
Who organized the tour, and how long was it?

items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Yeah. That was… I remember I took that job after Janie and I got married, ‘cause I’d been on the road so much and I thought, well, I can take a subway to work here and…

oh, what’s his name, the guitar player whose place I took? He was moving out to California. Can’t think of his name now. And… Yeah, so Bob (unintelligible) an incredible musician. Bob Brookmeyer. Richie Kamuca, marvelous tenor player. Art Davis, the bass player. Jake Hanna. Jake made it possible for… He was so funny. God. I would think… sometimes I would get so depressed doing it. ‘Cause I felt like I was… that’s one of the reasons I never got to record with Miles Davis. He, he had called me once before. Anyway,…
Bill Berry was in that group?
